review:
I really enjoyed this game. The art style immediately grabbed me with its distinctive vibe all the way through. Great characters and a genuinely interesting plot.
I thought the multi-tool could have been utilised more, especially since it was such a good idea for gameplay and the ending sequence felt a little rushed, but overall a very well crafted and executed game. Recommended!

Not so good, for a product that had 7 years to get polished.

Tried an achievement playthrough after completing this years ago on my previous account.
The Running Commentary doesn't even trigger, after that and the everbuilding annoyance it takes so f*cking long to exit the game plus Modern Man not triggering after doing everything right I will live the rest of my life in regret for spending money on giving this game another chance,

i'm working through it bit by bit, no hints no guide no nothing, and I find it very enjoyable so far. It's not necessarily easy and you may get stuck at times but not for too long. And the story is very intruiging, the game doesn't info-dump on you - so there's a real sense of mystery and of wanting to discover what's going on.
Good story. Not too boring, nice music and the atmosphere, most quests are logical. I enjoyed it :)

If you like old-style point-and-click style adventure games, this is a great one!  Good story and characters and great art.  The puzzles are challenging but not too opaque for the most part.  I got stuck sometimes, but usually in the good way that was fun when I figured it out.  There were only one or two places that I thought were unclear solutions, which I had to look up.

Lots of humor and fun to play.  The story has chapters and play is in different settings each chapter, so you don't get tired of walking around the same old place.  Highly recommend!

Played this a good few years ago but remember really enjoying it. Some of the puzzles or finding things were a little tricky but loved the story, voice acting and visual style. Have to do a replay sometime
good game very nice indeed

难度颇高的指向点击解谜，美漫手绘引起极度舒适。可能真反派在前期以纯洁无辜的形象多刷下存在感会更好，除了第四章篇幅较短收尾急了点没什么失误。

词汇量要求高，六级明显不够用。插科打诨式的幽默感是一大特色，使用了大量地道的俚语表达，英语非母语者会很难get到一些笑点。解谜非常难，难点不限于：道具的结合存在异想天开，对整张地图要有翻箱倒柜的细致搜索，谜题硬核写实，诸如野外生火、冲洗照片和破解电脑，甚至还要考验线索归纳和逻辑推演能力等。总之，本作需要沉下心来放慢节奏细细品味，至少得做好查攻略准备，这也是最大成本和劝退点了。

这个剧情嘛，简单来说就是各种刻板印象的集合了。首先是粗枝大叶修理工配心思缜密女记者，当然还有仿佛从《回到未来》穿越来的永远穿着白大褂的博士（全篇对这部电影有多处cue）；常把灵性智慧、精神能量挂在嘴边的往往是最在乎物质的偷鸡摸狗之人；对过往人生深恶痛绝的失败者和空怀满腔热血的年轻人，最容易被吸纳入邪教奉上虔诚信仰；反而是邪教头子对教义不屑一顾，全当作掌控力量的洗脑工具；能当上政客的必然要心狠手辣草菅人命；还有最经典的“扮英雄”手段，即先制造一场危机再向民众表演如何化解。尽管本作是从头典到尾了，能系统性风格化地凑成一本俗套教科书，读起来还是别有一番风味的。本作拿疫情做主题来讽刺，发售在全球新冠大流行之前，可以说是非常big胆和具备前瞻性了。 

男女主同款色系穿搭+不间断打情骂俏+发糖的理想结局=甜死我了。

The art style and dialogue were good, but the back and forth required to initiate dialogue and further clues was exhausting. Most of the game experience was back and forth which really disrupted the flow of the story. Would be better with a better flow of clues and linked dialogue rather than having to fish around for progression, especially in chapters where the clues were not very good at hinting at how to progress. I had to look up way too many assists to complete and then the story ended with a fizz and not a bang, rushed through in the last chapter. This would be better played as a 5hr game, but took 20hrs for me with all the back and forth...Not really worth the money it cost.

后两章解谜有点难度，总的来说很好玩，风格也好看的捏。
[spoiler] 交互确实很多，但能不能也让我吃吃三明治，我可以不要辣酱。 [/spoiler]

This is a truly impressive point-and-click adventure. There are a good variety of clever puzzles & mini-games without any of them feeling punishing and the art design and voice work are fantastic as well. The adventure was thrilling and the escalation of events was well paced, except maybe the ending. But the overall game was one of the best P&C games I have ever encountered.

A lot of the negative reviews are what I would say for most point and click games,  but not this one. I always have to look up a lot of stuff with point and click games because all the connections are always arbitrary or make no sense or I would never think of solving something that specific way the devs make you and always you just have to go back and forth over and over again to the same places. But not with this game, I found most of the puzzles made sense, there was minimal wandering and having to go back and forth. Still looked some stuff up (stupid harbor computer!!), but it turned out I was always going in the right direction and just needed an extra clue a handful of times. I think the negative reviews are too harsh, or people haven't played other point and clicks. This is another example of Steam needing a proper star rating or at least having a middle thumb.

I love the art direction, it's what made me get this game in the first place. I was also intrigued by the story in the trailer and it didn't dissapoint me the entire time I played. 

There are a lot of optimization issues like load screens taking a long time or being black for a while, or loading the main tool takes a second, or the zoom in when characters talk to each other has low res art. The low res bothered me the most, but at the same time....It's a studios first game and I've seen worse by bigger studios. 

The animation was obviously done by non-animators, the walk cycles are laughable. But honestly, even as an artist and animator myself, this didn't bother me too much since the animation is minimal and I liked so many other things about this game. I think this game was genuinely good. I liked the story and the art and the dialogue and the voice acting, it truly drew me in! Probably one of the best point and click games I've played in a long time.

art style is gorgeous but the plot so far is just meh. far too many unfunny quips and extremely flat characters. the "puzzles" are just a bunch of incredibly tedious fetch quests, and the story isn't engaging enough to make me feel like slogging through them for any longer. I only got to triangulating the signal and I don't think I'll be playing any further.

It's not an awful game, I just don't like it.

You know those "funny" remarks in point and click games when you click something irrelevant? Yeah, this game is chock-full of them.

There's no hint system, the solutions are a bit vague, the problems themselves are vague, (what do I even do next?) you go about same places a lot, the characters are a bit off, the artstyle is eh...

All in all, it's not awful, but none of it is very good.

Vor sechs Jahren hatte ich Unforeseen Incidents etwa halb durchgespielt, dann brutal tagelang festgehangen, und aufgegeben. Walkthroughs hatte ich nicht bemühen wollen. Das war ein Fehler. 

Das Spiel hat mindestens zwei unlogische Stellen, die durch irreführende Hinweise begleitet kaum zu lösen sind. Was auch daran liegt, dass die Größe des Problemfeldes zeitweise ins Unüberschaubare ausartet. Deshalb sollte man notfalls Hilfe annehmen, dann erweist sich das Spiel als großartiges Adventure. 

Und so habe ich das Spiel jetzt noch einmal von vorne begonnen, mir insgesamt dreimal helfen lassen, und es letztlich sehr genossen. Auch alle Achievements erreicht. Die Atmosphäre des Spiels, seine Rätsel, die Zeichnungen, die Musik und Geräusche, sehr gut. Über die Animationen der laufenden Personen schweigt des Sängers Höflichkeit. Wer's noch nicht gespielt hat - nicht entgehen lassen!
Fantastic game! The puzzles are mostly great (with a few confusing item-linked exceptions), but overall a great time.
Сюжет интересный, рисовка очень интересная, загадки не слишком простые, заглядывал в прохождение несколько раз.
This game has some of the most well-written dialogue I've seen. It's very naturally funny without trying too hard, and the voice acting on it is spot on, especially from the main character.

Unforseen Incidents hat mich gleich in mehrere Hinsicht positiv überrascht. Die Hintergründe und die Figuren heben sich von ihrem Zeichenstil her deutlich von anderen Point-and-Click-Adventures ab. Visuell eine helle Freude, die von der Tonspur und der großartigen Synchronisation unterstützt wird. Das alles trägt sehr gut zur Atmosphäre bei und unterstützt das Storytelling. Der Protagonist und die Rätsel sind erfrischend anders, dazu kommt eine ausgewogene Balance zwischen Humor und Spannung. Das Spiel läuft sehr flüssig und ist insgesamt schlüssig. Hoffentlich gibt es bald ein neues Spiel von Backwoods Entertainment!

Unfortunately the game seems to be quite buggy. In the first chapter the game corrupted the save file, so that you can not interact with the mouse again and are stuck in the current view of the level. Since there are no frequent auto-saves basically an hour of playtime is lost, which does not make me want to continue the game.
Lovely atmosphere and characters. Nice riddles and good soundtrack.

I enjoyed playing this game! Funky little art style that complemented the humor. Lovely musical score that did so much heavy lifting in setting the correct mood. 

Would have loved to go maybe one layer deeper with all the NPCs -- they felt like they were there to serve their purpose and that's it. With the story line being what it is, I felt it was a missed opportunity to use some of that great dialogue to support the impact of the conspiracy bubbling beneath the surface. Especially in the initial area, Yelltown -- I wanted my heart to break during the Act 1 reveal, but we didn't develop enough of a connection with the NPCs for that to happen. I felt bad for them, but there was room to make me feel devastated.

The ending felt a little rushed, but I think you stuck the landing (albeit with a little wobble). 

Fun puzzles and I only got stuck twice, because I didn't realize you could examine/comment on object in the inventory (there are a couple areas where this locks you from moving forward until you get Harper to look at the item and say what he needs to say about it, even if it's obvious where to use it next). 

All in all, I really liked this game. And it was oddly prescient considering the year it was released. Definitely recommend.

Nettes Point&Click mit mystischer Atmosphäre.
Klasse Synchro mit vielen doppelten Aufnahmen für jedes Objekt.

Great game! Enjoyed it thoroughly! Loved the characters and the plot. The art style is awesome, and I really vibed with the lore and worldbuilding in general. The voice actors did an amazing job too! Personally, I found the puzzles weren't too hard but also not too easy. What I enjoyed most about the game is probably the soundtrack itself—it fit so well with the world and plot. Apart from a few visual glitches and lines where the voiceovers were not triggered, I didn't run into any issues. The only thing I found a little strange was that the ending felt a little rushed compared to the previous chapters. There are also a few loose ends that I wish they tied together, but overall this game has earned a soft spot in my heart! I highly recommend it. :)

This game is not that interesting, but if you're a fan of classic point and click adventure games like the Monkey Island series, then it's worth a playthrough. It's not super hard, but also probably not super friendly to newcomers of the genre (i.e., not like The Drifter, which was way too easy).

The puzzles in this game are medium-level difficulty for an adventure game. I was never really stuck for very long.

As far as adventure games go, the storyline is okay. The characters and VA are okay. The main character is so mid - you don't feel anything towards him. Also the dialogue is not funny. So being not funny + not interesting storyline and mid puzzles make for a super-mid game.

I finished it b/c I love adventure games. And also maybe takes place in Canada (?), which is a plus in my books. The art and environments are pretty nice, easy on the eyes, but not necessarily amazing.

The game is kinda janky, it lags a lot at times, especially after it's been running for a while. I feel like it's not optimized properly. It does not have cloud saves, which is annoying if you switch computers frequently. Luckily you can jump to chapters, so it's good enough to continue and/or achievement hunt.

The achievements are okay, there are some missables, which require a bit of replay, but nothing crazy.

I loved the story, the characters, and animation style of this game and I would love another game with a continuation of the main characters on another adventure or investigation. The voice acting was also really above par. I find myself wishing I was playing this while playing less immersive point and clicks.
My only note would be that it is frustrating that you can't (or at least i couldn't figure out how to) pause the game while it's in the middle of a dialogue tree or an npc character speech. This meant that if I got suddenly pulled away from my computer or distracted for a moment there was no easy pause and I would miss the conversation or speech, and was unable to replay it unless I wanted to start the entire game chapter all over again, which I of course did not. While this didn't make or break any gameplay, as someone who was enjoying the actual story plot it was a little frustrating.
Eerily prophetic.  I played this game during the early 2020 lockdowns and it creeped me out in the best possible way!

I love the atmosphere of this game ,as well as the feelings of being unforeseen,unpredictable,intense,mysterious.

The puzzles are easy and creative,whats interesting is that the rigid yet elastic puzzle-solving with intense story,the puzzles are tightly combined with the fragmented narrative, it creates an immersive narrative.

GAME: Solid and funny adventure title. Memorable characters, super cool artstyle, and nice atmospheric soundtrack. Story itself was only so-so for me personally (a little generic and predictable), but I did enjoy the different locations you go to and interactions. Puzzles were pretty fun to figure out, though I did have to consult a walkthrough a couple times. 

**ISSUES**: Unfortunately I also did encounter several bugs while playing (cursor issues, progression/cutscene not triggering) and the only solution I found was to switch to a different save file. Therefore I HIGHLY recommend creating many different saves in your playthrough. And if you play on an ultra-wide, you WILL need to switch the resolution to a regular 16:9 ratio (important aspects will get cut off in ultrawide). There are no resolution settings in-game, instead hold "alt" key while launching the game from steam, and that will bring up a popup to let you change the resolution.

CAUTION - Minor Spoilers on Plot Structure

This would be a good game but everything your character does is negated at the end of each chapter by some silly plot contrivance.  It's very frustrating and just doesn't make the game feel satisfying at all.  I do think the puzzles are good and logical, just not enough to overcome the lack of feeling of progress.

I'd recommend it, but if I were to rate it I'd give it a 7/10. The story itself was very intriguing, and I quite enjoyed most of the puzzles. There were some parts that had me scratching my head at how I'm meant to solve them, and I did have to refer to a walkthrough once or twice because certain solutions just did not seem to be the logical choice, but I feel most games in the point n click genre tend to do that. There were a couple glitches like certain items not leaving your inventory after you had used it, but those small bits were pretty negligible in terms of my enjoyment of the game. The thing that I dislike most is that the ending was pretty disappointing. There was this whole exciting, intriguing build-up all throughout the game, and the reveal and climax were awesome! But then when it came time for the wrap-up... it just did not feel like any of the story had really paid off.

Overall, this was a pretty fun adventure game! Maybe not at the top of my list for point n click games, but it certainly was an enjoyable experience.

并不是一个一无是处的游戏，我特别喜欢每一章开头的新闻广播过场，游戏配音确实出色，不仅是角色全配音，比如书本翻页、烧开水、开窗、开车等等的都有音效。角色、美术和配乐其实都是加分项，剧情合格线之上，但在没有翻译的加持下，糟糕的游戏交互和过于折腾的跑腿、解谜实在太消磨游戏热情了。

游戏背景是城市突然爆发神秘病毒疫情，防疫公司呼吁大家互相警惕，遇到可能患病的人就及时打电话送入研究所隔离。游戏中虽然这个传染病让人人心惶惶，到处是穿着防疫服的黄衣人，但也正巧有一场盛大的球赛直播正在进行中，主角在路上遇到了一个病倒在地的女人，她阻止了主角试图救助打电话还塞给他一封信交给某个记者，这封信也将引导他和女记者一起追寻整个城镇疫情的真相与出路。游戏倒是在新冠疫情之前出的，但面对游戏中一些讽刺和描述还是感觉微妙地搞笑。

后期涉及什么商战阴谋论那些实在太老套了，解谜体验更加差，有非常多意图明显的跨地图跑腿任务，且每个机密关卡对道具要求非常严苛，说好听点这是所有道具都有用处，但反过来说意味着如果你之前错过了某个关键工具（比如前期你翻垃圾桶捡一对被丢弃的丝袜）没拿或者卡BUG了，那除非你重新跑回去拿（很大可能是你甚至不知道缺了什么在哪拿）整个游戏就无法进行了。最无语的是男主自带的多功能工具操作起来很麻烦，时常卡顿不说每次使用还需要选用哪种功能；后期还出现某个关卡解锁密码提示词甚至是不限字数输入一种“羞辱的话”，完全靠词汇量硬猜，不看攻略一辈子想不出来。

总之在这种解谜推进剧情步步为营又没有代入感，且结局单一的游戏，真好奇故事还不如云算了。

Unforeseen Incidents is a beautifully crafted point-and-click adventure game that captures the spirit of classic narrative-driven mysteries while infusing it with modern sensibilities and stunning hand-painted visuals. Developed by Backwoods Entertainment, this title stands out in the adventure genre through its compelling storytelling, well-designed puzzles, and atmospheric world-building. From the moment you step into the shoes of Harper Pendrell, a down-on-her-luck handyman caught in a mysterious epidemic sweeping through a small town, the game offers a rich narrative experience filled with intrigue, emotional depth, and thoughtful character development.

The story unfolds in a small, seemingly quiet town suddenly disrupted by a strange and deadly virus outbreak. Harper, tasked with helping friends and neighbors while unraveling the larger conspiracy behind the infection, finds herself entangled in a web of secrets involving corporate malfeasance, government cover-ups, and ethical dilemmas. The writing is one of Unforeseen Incidents’ greatest strengths; it balances tension, mystery, and humor in a way that feels both engaging and grounded. The dialogue is sharp, with natural-sounding exchanges that bring the characters to life, making every interaction meaningful. The game also thoughtfully explores themes of trust, responsibility, and the human impact of crises, which adds a layer of depth beyond the typical adventure game fare.

Gameplay-wise, Unforeseen Incidents adheres to classic point-and-click conventions but with a polished and accessible interface. Players explore various interconnected environments, interact with objects, gather clues, and solve puzzles that are intelligently designed and woven seamlessly into the story. The puzzles are challenging without being frustrating, often requiring keen observation and creative problem-solving. Unlike many adventure games that rely on obscure item combinations or arbitrary logic, Unforeseen Incidents encourages players to think critically and pay close attention to their surroundings, making the experience feel rewarding and fair.

The game’s hand-painted art style deserves special mention. Each scene is richly detailed and atmospheric, with a warm, muted color palette that perfectly complements the game’s tone—sometimes somber, sometimes hopeful. The environments feel lived-in and believable, from cozy homes to eerie laboratories, enhancing immersion and emotional resonance. Character portraits and animations, while subtle, effectively convey emotions and personality, further drawing players into the narrative. The sound design and musical score work in tandem with the visuals to create a moody, suspenseful atmosphere that heightens the tension and complements the unfolding mystery.

One of the notable features of Unforeseen Incidents is its pacing. The game carefully balances moments of intense investigation and puzzle-solving with quieter scenes that allow for character development and world exploration. This rhythm prevents fatigue and keeps players invested in both the mystery and the emotional journeys of the characters. Moreover, the game offers multiple locations to explore, each with its own secrets and story beats, encouraging thorough exploration and rewarding curiosity.

While Unforeseen Incidents excels in many areas, it is not without minor flaws. Some players might find certain puzzles slightly too straightforward, reducing the challenge for seasoned adventure gamers. Conversely, a few moments could feel a bit slow due to the deliberate pacing or the amount of dialogue, which might test the patience of those seeking faster action or more dynamic gameplay. However, these are relatively minor quibbles in the context of a narrative experience focused on atmosphere and storytelling.

Overall, Unforeseen Incidents is a standout title for fans of story-driven adventure games. It offers a mature, thought-provoking narrative wrapped in an elegant artistic package, with puzzles and gameplay mechanics that honor the tradition of the genre while feeling fresh and accessible. The game’s rich world, memorable characters, and emotional depth make it more than just a mystery—it’s an immersive journey that challenges players to think critically about the story’s ethical questions while enjoying a beautifully realized interactive experience. For anyone who appreciates well-crafted narratives and immersive puzzle-solving in a captivating setting, Unforeseen Incidents is a game worth playing.

Unforeseen Incidents nous propose une aventure à l’ancienne avec un jeu de style point & click qui fera plaisir aux nostalgiques. Les puzzles seront intéressants et logiques, le jeu demande de réfléchir, de combiner des objets et de bien écouter les dialogues. 

On ne ferait pas un bon point & click sans une histoire palpitante. Sur ce point, le jeu s’en sort avec la moyenne. Le scénario, mêlant épidémie mystérieuse, complot à grande échelle et secte de fanatiques, est agréable à suivre bien que les quelques twists soient attendus et ne viennent pas réellement nous surprendre. La touche d’humour dans les dialogues et le côté décalé que prend notre personnage apporte une légèreté bienvenue malgré des thèmes somme toute assez lourds.  

Le titre jouit d’une jolie direction artistique avec des dessins réalisés à la main d’une patte reconnaissable. Il a ainsi sa propre identité et c’est son atout le plus marqué. Aussi, Unforeseen Incidents s’offre des doublages en anglais de bonne qualité, participant à l’immersion. On pourra regretter qu’un délai parfois trop important vient souvent s'intercaler entre deux répliques, rendant le dialogue robotique.

Sur Steam Deck, pensez à installer la configuration de touches “point & click” de la communauté, permettant d’utiliser le pavé tactile et de cliquer avec la gâchette. Les contrôles de base ne sont ni agréables ni adaptés à un jeu sur console portable. Attention aussi à un bug qui peut être très embêtant, j’ai par deux fois eu mon curseur qui restait sous forme de croix et ne me permettait plus de cliquer nulle part. La première fois, j’ai pu recharger une partie. La seconde, je venais malheureusement de sauvegarder lorsque le bug est survenu. Je ne saurai expliquer réellement ce qui m’a débloqué mais j’ai persisté pendant un temps à essayer de me dépatouiller de cette situation. Il aurait fallu recommencer le jeu si je n’y parvenais pas, aïe. 

Unforeseen Incidents n’est pas un jeu marquant ou qui s’illustre avec un scénario de dingue. Non. Néanmoins, suivre l’enquête est intéressant, les puzzles ponctuent bien l’aventure et les dessins soignés suffisent à nous accrocher. C’est une bonne pioche pour les fondus du genre.
